text: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
mechanism: Every candidate is under-trained, so loss falls monotonically with how far parameters move from init; adaptive optimizers move ~lr per step regardless of gradient scale, so lr·T measures distance. Predicts the rule saturates once Δ is enough to fit the (tiny, noiseless) train set (~0.1-0.3), after which overconfidence/overshoot dominates - observed in the phase table.
phase: Largest-Δ (≥3× gap) win rate depends on the smaller Δ: <0.03 ~95% (tabular lab 2011/2135); 0.03-0.1 ~60-88%; once smaller Δ≥0.1 only 25-60% (bigram 25%, tabular 43%, spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58%, univariate 60%; K1012, K1021). LR-ceiling breaks: K1004.

text: BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.
mechanism: Labels are sampled from P(y|x), so minibatch gradients carry irreducible noise; with a constant lr, once the V×V table is fit further displacement only adds noise-driven parameter jitter and memorisation of the 800 training windows (positions/contexts), raising test CE. More parameters per token (d_model 128) reach that fit point at smaller Δ, so the optimum shifts down with width - predicting d128 < d64 ≈ d32 optimum, as observed.

regime.note: same model within set; V 24-48, alpha 0.8-1.4, 800 windows, bs16; Δ<0.03 rivals: max-Δ applies

text: BIGRAM LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): decide by the shared core-rule Δ band. Δ<0.02 (nearly frozen: Adam-family ≤3e-5 at T≤512, SGD ≤3e-3): GRU wins, even vs larger d_model when alpha≤1 (corpus 8/8, controlled GRU 5/6; q_5e328e GRU64×2 beat d128). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: a transformer of EQUAL or LARGER d_model wins (lab GRU 1/20; controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9 at every T 256-2048; q_9344eb GRU64×2 last at AdamW 3e-5×2048, even below d32×3 d_ff256); GRU64 vs d32: GRU 9/9 observational, lean GRU only if 1-layer. 0.1≤Δ<0.5: GRU wins 8/9 (any d_model). Δ≥0.5: GRU 3/3 (transformer overshoots, K1071).
mechanism: Both nets must learn a current-token lookup. When nearly frozen, the GRU's gates pass the input embedding straight to the output, so tiny updates already cut CE, while the transformer must first beat random positional embeddings and attention mixing. Once Δ≥0.02 the transformer's residual stream carries token identity and its FF fits the table faster than a 2-layer non-residual GRU; by Δ≥0.1 post-LN transformers overshoot (K1071), returning the edge to the GRU.

regime.note: alpha 0.8-1.4, V 24-48, L 12-24; GRUs non-residual d32/d64; Δ 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 cells small (9, 3 pairs)

phase: GRU win rate: Δ<0.02 corpus 8/8, lab 1/2, controlled 5/6; 0.02-0.1 equal/larger-d transformer: lab 1/20, controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9, 1-layer 3/9; GRU d>T d 9/9 obs; 0.1-0.5 8/9; ≥0.5 3/3. Flip between Δ 0.015 and 0.05.
